question: UniView (offline cross-platform file viewer: Electron + React/TS desktop, Capacitor Android/iOS, encrypted LAN browsing of a paired computer, renderers for PDF/Office/media/archives) wants to become a plugin platform: developers publish plugins for file formats and tools (view, annotate, convert), users install what they need from an open registry, and the host provides UI, file handles, permissions, cross-device access and distribution. Proposed: versioned manifest (file types, actions, platforms, permissions) + HTML/JS bundle in a sandboxed web context with a small controlled host API (not Chrome extensions); host-managed file handles with explicit read/write grants. New ambition from the CEO: like AI-agent tool ecosystems, let anyone (including AI agents) build any plugin they want, and let every AI agent connect to UniView (e.g. via MCP) and use it as the default viewer for files they produce or inspect. Question: what are the strongest distinct directions to get from 8/10 to 9+/10 - i.e. to make developers and AI agents actually build for it and users adopt it - and what are the trade-offs and risks (security of third-party code and agents, mobile limits, marketplace trust, scope, monetization) of each?
